title: The SessionStart intake hook files a finding once, whatever checkout or session starts, and respects the open-draft cap
goal: backlog.py intake --file --hook writes no draft for a fingerprint that an untracked draft, a committed item or a draft set aside under _cache/intake-drafts/ of the clone's main worktree already holds, and writes none while open drafts are at the cap (bl_intake.OPEN_DRAFTS_MAX) the CLI form enforces, with no near-duplicate merge; in SP-7y6dk257 the hook re-filed the same three findings 11 times and then 3 more after they were set aside, while intake --file refused them for the 60-draft cap. In a linked worktree under .claude/worktrees/ its one stderr line names the worktree (its directory name) as the reason it files nothing, where _tools/bl_ci.py prints a fixed string (found by the SP-gkbtjjce review). Retrospective of SP-7y6dk257.

run: import tempfile,subprocess,sys,os;d=tempfile.mkdtemp();g=lambda *a,c=d:subprocess.run(['git','-c','user.name=t','-c','user.email=t@t','-C',c,*a],capture_output=True,text=True);g('init','-q');g('commit','-q','--allow-empty','-m','x');w=d+'/.claude/worktrees/w1';g('worktree','add','-q','-b','b1',w);os.makedirs(w+'/kb/_self/backlog',exist_ok=True);p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,os.getcwd()+'/_tools/backlog.py','--root',w,'intake','--file','--hook'],capture_output=True,text=True);ok=p.returncode==0 and 'w1' in p.stderr;print('intake exit',p.returncode,'stderr:',p.stderr.strip() or 'empty','| names the worktree:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

gates.question: What does the SessionStart intake hook enforce before it files a draft: only the open-draft cap, or also the near-duplicate merge intake --file runs?

Where does the hook look for a draft that already holds a fingerprint: this checkout's items and the set-aside directory of the clone's main worktree, or also the untracked drafts of every linked worktree?
Which committed items' fingerprints stop the SessionStart intake hook from filing a draft?

notes: Merged from BG-eam5x2q7 (the stderr line names the worktree; its repro is the second check) at the 2026-10-10 backlog triage. The hook is hook_intake in _tools/bl_ci.py: it skips only a fingerprint an open item of this checkout holds (open_with_fingerprint) and never counts the cap that bl_intake.file_draft enforces. INTAKE_ASIDE lives in bl_land.py and bl_ci.py must not import bl_land (layer rule), so the constant moves to bl_intake.py and bl_land.py imports it. The -k selector names a test yet to write: tests.py exits 2 until the work adds it. Planned at the 2026-10-10 whole-backlog triage, which the operator asked to end with every draft planned into a sprint or dropped (sprint 5 of 13, "Headless sprint loop 2: intake drafts, land windows and worker cost"); the triage reviewer found it serves the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test F2: a content sprint from the research queue lands on headless Sonnet workers. Premise run at planning (2026-10-10): grep -c for OPEN_DRAFTS_MAX, INTAKE_ASIDE, intake-drafts and open_drafts in _tools/bl_ci.py prints 0, so hook_intake neither counts the cap nor reads the aside directory; the second check's repro exits 1 (stderr is a fixed string): reproduces.
